subject: Discovery recap: model runbook, recommended slate, and Redwood perf evidence
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@optilex.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 16:10:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap: model runbook, recommended slate, and Redwood perf evidence

Julia — thanks again for a focused call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can keep momentum toward a 4-week pilot.

High-level fit notes
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + triage routing (short-to-medium context, 256-1024 tokens).
- Quality SLO: 95% acceptable summary rate on optilex internal eval set; regression tolerance: no more than 3% drop vs your current baseline.

Recommended model slate (shortlist we ran locally + Redwood-verified profiles)
1) open-instruct-XXL (quantized, Redwood profile A) — highest-quality candidate for capturing instruction fine-grain; good p50 but heavier cost.
2) rdx-chat-13b (q4f) — balanced quality/cost; strong prefix/cache benefits for repeated support prompts.
3) rdx-7b-llm-low-lat (distilled + kernel-tuned) — lower cost, good for high-concurrency routing/triage.

What we measured (Redwood-verified profiles) — included full traces and configs in attachments/links
- open-instruct-XXL: sustained 60 TPS (single A100-80GB), p50=120ms, p95=420ms at 512-token responses (batch=1 continuous batching).
- rdx-chat-13b (q4f): sustained 200 TPS (2xA100 mixed), p50=85ms, p95=260ms for 256-token median responses.
- rdx-7b-llm-low-lat: sustained 450 TPS (optimized kernel on 2xT4), p50=35ms, p95=110ms for short responses (128 tokens).

Attachments and artifacts
- optilex_bench_v1.csv (raw run-level samples + latency histogram)
- redwood_perf_report_optilex.pdf (summary, config snippets for kernel selection, batching settings, and KV-cache usage)
- Perf JSON: s3://redwood-evals/optilex/2026-07-20/perf.json

Quality regression concerns we flagged during evaluation
- prompt-sensitivity: open-instruct-XXL shows occasional hallucination on very terse prompts; we propose a 10-example prompt guard (attached prompt_set_v1.txt) and a lightweight QA reranker to reduce false positives.
- drift on entity normalization in triage — suggested guardrails: canonicalization step in prompt + a small post-processing rule set.

Suggested pilot runbook (what we can provide in the pilot)
- Phase 0 (1 week): ingest prompt sets + NR (noisy-real) samples; deploy rdx-chat-13b with prefix caching, warm KV cache; smoke tests.
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): A/B: rdx-chat-13b vs rdx-7b-low-lat; collect latency/quality signals and run regression checks against your golden set.
- Phase 2 (1 week): wrap up, recommend final model + quantization profile and hand over optimization suggestions for Dedicated/Private deployment.

Pricing / capacity ask
- To hit the above: recommend 2xA100 (rdx-chat-13b) + 2xT4 (rdx-7b) as the pilot baseline. Ben will follow up on a firm pilot quote.

Next steps / asks
1) Julia — confirm 1) pilot scope (A/B) and 2) approval to share the eval artifacts internally (procurement) so we can attach an SOW.
2) I will push the RW perf-report link and attach the sample prompt pack.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: model runbook, recommended slate, and Redwood perf evidence

Julia / team — quick technical runbook and a tightened pilot option to meet your p95 < 300ms routing constraint.

Tightened pilot (cost-savings): start with rdx-7b-low-lat as primary + rdx-chat-13b as fallback for a small % of traffic (5–10%) to protect quality. This reduces steady state GPU need to 2xT4 (primary) + 1xA100 (fallback warm) — estimated pilot cost ~$9.5k–$12k with same one-time eval tooling fee.

Runbook (configuration snippets)
- Inference config: continuous batching bucket 50ms, max_batch_size 64; prefix KV cache enabled for repeated threads; token limit = 1024 (config attached in perf PDF).
- Latency guard: implement an adaptive fallback policy — if p50 of a short-window (1 min) exceeds 120ms, route to rdx-7b and raise the per-request priority header for downstream logging.
- Regression checks: daily QC job (nightly) that runs 500 held-out prompts; alert triggers if BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxy drops > 2.5% or hallucination metric moves +3%.

Operational asks from OptiLex
1) Redacted CSV (mask customer IDs) — we can work with that for benchmarking.
2) Test token budget: please confirm expected daily requests (est. 50k/day used for these numbers).
3) NDA/SOW contact for procurement to receive line-item pricing (Ben + Legal).

I'll prepare a compact pilot SOW and a playground link that spins up the baseline config for you to smoke-test.

If that sounds good, Ben — can you convert to a one-page SOW and loop procurement? Julia — if you approve redaction and the tightened pilot option, reply with a thumbs up and I'll push the playground.

— Vivek
